title: Micah 4:1–5
context: After the sentence on Zion, Micah sees that in the latter days the mountain of the LORD’s temple will be raised above the hills and peoples will stream to it to learn his ways; the LORD will judge between nations, and swords will become plowshares (4:1–3). Micah 4:1–3 closely parallels Isaiah 2:2–4, with differences in wording that are noted without harmonizing; Micah adds the picture of each person under vine and fig tree (4:4) and closes with a confession of walking in the LORD’s name (4:5), where Isaiah 2:5 calls Jacob to walk in the LORD’s light. Readers in both traditions take the vision as fulfilled in Christ and the spread of the gospel, as a picture of the church, or as awaiting a future fulfillment; see the existing Isaiah 2:2 box.

verses.text: But in the latter days, it will happen that the mountain of the LORD’s temple will be established on the top of the mountains, and it will be exalted above the hills; and peoples will stream to it.
verses.arminianNotes: “But in the latter days,” “the mountain of the LORD’s temple will be established on the top of the mountains” Arminian readers commonly hear the times of the Messiah, with nations streaming to God’s word.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers likewise commonly hear the kingdom of Christ, begun and yet to be completed. Micah 4:1–3 closely parallels Isaiah 2:2–4, with differences in wording that are noted without harmonizing; the Isaiah 2:2 box sets out how each tradition reads the latter days.

verses.text: Many nations will go and say, “Come! Let’s go up to the mountain of the LORD, and to the house of the God of Jacob; and he will teach us of his ways, and we will walk in his paths.” For the law will go out of Zion, and the LORD’s word from Jerusalem;
verses.arminianNotes: Many nations say, “Come! Let’s go up to the mountain of the LORD.” Arminian readers see nations freely coming to learn God’s ways, drawn by his word going out from Zion.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers likewise see the nations gathered by the word that goes out from Jerusalem. Shared ground: God teaches, and the peoples walk in his paths; readers in both traditions commonly hear the spread of the gospel here.

verses.text: and he will judge between many peoples, and will decide concerning strong nations afar off. They will beat their swords into plowshares, and their spears into pruning hooks. Nation will not lift up sword against nation, neither will they learn war any more.
verses.arminianNotes: “They will beat their swords into plowshares, and their spears into pruning hooks.” Arminian readers see the peace that comes when the LORD judges between nations.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers likewise see peace as the fruit of God’s reign. Joel 3:10 reverses the image, and readers in this tradition hold historic, typological, and future readings of the promised peace within the same tradition.

verses.text: But every man will sit under his vine and under his fig tree. No one will make them afraid, for the mouth of the LORD of Armies has spoken.
verses.arminianNotes: “But every man will sit under his vine and under his fig tree. No one will make them afraid.” Arminian readers see security and contentment for ordinary families, an addition not found in Isaiah 2.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers likewise see the image of peace from Solomon’s days (1 Kings 4:25). Shared ground: the promise rests on “the mouth of the LORD of Armies,” and its fulfillment depends on his word.

verses.text: Indeed all the nations may walk in the name of their gods, but we will walk in the name of the LORD our God forever and ever.
verses.arminianNotes: “Indeed all the nations may walk in the name of their gods, but we will walk in the name of the LORD our God forever.” Arminian readers see the faithful choosing to walk with the LORD now.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers likewise see a confession of loyalty in the present while the vision awaits fulfillment. Isaiah 2:5 closes the parallel differently, and readers in this tradition note the difference without harmonizing.
